title: Log morning run to Notion Workout Log via audio upload
breadth_reason: This script tests the ability to process a health/logging intent via uploaded audio and execute a CRM action on Notion, expanding beyond simple note-taking to structured database entry.

v7_target.engine: user-device engine installed on user's computer
v7_target.surface_rule: User's Chrome with signed-in Notion and a visible database table
v7_target.proof_rule: ASR transcript from uploaded audio must match expected spoken reference text, and Notion surface must be verifiably visible in the user's active browser

primary_user_input.reason: Uploaded audio provides a reliable ASR path without requiring live microphone access, covering the user's intent via a single artifact.

real_user_surfaces.name: Notion Workout Log database
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: visible database table with columns for date, duration, distance, tags, and a row for today's entry

real_user_surfaces.name: Signed-in Chrome profile
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: confirmed signed-in Notion account within the Chrome profile

moments.description: User navigates to https://www.anticipy.ai/app, completes sign-in and onboarding, downloads the public installer, and installs the user-device engine on their computer.
Engine verifies that the user's Chrome has a signed-in Notion session and that a database table (Workout Log) is visible in a browser tab.

moments.spoken_reference_text: Please add a new record to my Notion Workout Log database for today's morning run, forty five minutes, four point two miles, and tag it long-run. If you cannot prove the visible Notion surface or my signed-in workspace, decline without writing anything.
moments.delivery_instruction: User uploads an MP3 audio file via /api/listen/upload. The engine transcribes it and compares to the spoken_reference_text.

moments.description: After ASR, engine checks that the transcript matches the expected reference text and that the Notion surface is still visible and valid.

acceptable_outcomes: act: add a new record to the Notion Workout Log database with the specified fields
ask: prompt user to confirm if the surface is ambiguous or missing required columns
decline: refuse to write if the Notion surface is not verifiably visible or user is not signed in

moments.description: This script does not rely on transcript paste or live microphone; uploaded audio is the only primary path. Other modes are listed as not_primary to ensure the system prioritizes audio upload for ASR verification.

success_criteria: The engine successfully processes the uploaded audio and extracts the intent to log a workout.
A new record is added to the Notion Workout Log database with fields: date (today), duration (45 minutes), distance (4.2 miles), and tag (long-run).
The engine confirms the Notion surface is visible and signed-in using the user's real Chrome profile.
If the surface is not verifiable, the engine declines without writing any data.
The entire flow uses only the primary input mode (uploaded audio) and does not fallback to transcript paste or live capture.
failure_triggers: If the uploaded audio file is corrupted or not in valid MP3 format, the ASR fails and the engine declines.
If the Notion surface is not open or the user is not signed in, the engine declines without creating a record.
If the ASR transcript does not match the expected spoken reference text (e.g., wrong duration or missing tag), the engine prompts for clarification or declines.
If the user attempts to use transcript paste or live mic as the primary input, the engine ignores them and only accepts uploaded audio.
If the Chrome profile cannot be verified as the user's signed-in profile, the engine declines.
